subject: Demo recap + proposed activation path — POC readiness
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@brightbridge.com>, Tomas Green <tomas.green@brightbridge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 16:09:00 -0700
Subject: Demo recap + proposed activation path — POC readiness

Hi Emily and Tomas,

Thanks again for taking time earlier today — great conversation. Quick recap from our side and a proposed activation path so we can get a short POC moving next week if that still works for the team.

What we heard:
- Goal: Reduce triage time for customer support queries and create a reliable summary + suggested action pipeline for agents.
- Success criteria (your proposed): 30% reduction in mean time to resolution on triaged tickets; summaries judged >=80% helpful by a 3-person QA panel; no PHI leakage.
- Minimum viable scope for POC: 1 month, 5k ticket/day sample from two support queues (billing + technical), Redwood hosted environment with enterprise logging and audit.

Proposed POC activation path (high level):
1) Agreement & scope sign-off (3 business days) — finalize data extracts and retention window.
2) Tech kickoff (day 1) — shared S3 location + credentials, security questionnaire outstanding items (we will provide SOC2 evidence).
3) Baseline run (days 2–7) — ingest 1 week of historic tickets to measure baseline MTR and summary quality.
4) Iteration & tuning (weeks 2–3) — prompt engineering, batching/latency tuning, model selection (open/quantized variants).
5) Acceptance gate (end of week 4) — evaluate against the success criteria above and decide next steps (extend to staging or roll to pilot).

Owners (initial):
- Redwood: Sofia (technical lead / integration) + Marissa (CS owner / success metrics).
- Brightbridge: Emily (product sponsor) + Tomas (data & infra lead).

Open questions / asks for your team to confirm:
- Can Brightbridge share a 7–14 day sample export (CSV or S3) for the two queues by Friday?
- Any legal/compliance contacts to include on the kickoff invite?
- Do you have a preferred NDA/PO template or should we send ours?

Attachments: POC checklist (spreadsheet) + proposed POC one-pager (PDF) — both attached.

If this looks good I can send a calendar hold for a tech kickoff early next week and loop in our security SME.

Thanks,
Sofia Ivanova
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Hi Sofia — thanks for the clear note. This captures everything we discussed. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Data: We can export a 10-day sample for the two queues and drop it into an S3 bucket (we'll send credentials). Can you confirm the schema you need?
2) PHI: our legal team will require a short data flow diagram and a statement that Redwood will not preserve raw ticket text beyond the POC retention window.
3) Timeline: Friday works for the sample; can we start the tech kickoff on Monday 5 April at 10am PT?

Also, Tomas asked whether Redwood can recommend a quantized model variant — low-latency is important for us.

We'll loop in Legal (CC'd after internal alignment).

Best,

Hi Emily — perfect, thanks. Quick answers inline:

1) Schema: CSV with columns (ticket_id, created_at, queue, text_body, attachments_count, user_id). If S3, please put files under s3://brightbridge-data/redwood-poc/<date> and share a short manifest (we can accept compressed files).
2) PHI / retention: We will provide a data flow diagram and commit to a 30-day deletion policy for raw ticket text from our hosted trial environment; we can also support a customer-managed encryption key. I'll have our security SME add the diagram to the kickoff deck.
3) Tech kickoff: Monday 2027-04-05 10:00 AM PT works for us — I'll send a calendar invite with agenda.

Model recommendation: For low-latency production-like tests we'd typically start with an 8-bit quantized Llama-2.1 variant or a distilled open model (we'll bring two recommended variants to the baseline run and measure latency/quality tradeoffs).

Next steps from here (I will action):
- Send calendar invite for 2027-04-05 10:00 AM PT with agenda and pre-kickoff checklist (today).
- Share an abbreviated data flow diagram / SOC2 evidence link for your legal review (tomorrow).
- Confirm S3 manifest format for your exports (today).

Thanks — looking forward to getting started.
Sofia

Hi Emily/Tomas — Marissa here (Customer Success). Wanted to introduce myself and confirm I'll run the acceptance evaluation at the end of week 4.

My plan for acceptance checkpoints: 
- Week 1: Baseline metrics validated (MTR, volume sanity checks).
- Week 2: Interim quality review — 50-sample manual review with weighted rubric (helpfulness, correctness, redaction).
- Week 3: Latency/stability gating (95th pct latency under target for your queues).
- Week 4: Final acceptance — aggregated metrics and QA panel decision.

Deliverables I'll produce: acceptance playbook (spreadsheet), weekly progress notes, and a short readout deck at the end of the POC.

I've added a short acceptance checklist to the POC checklist attachment and will include owners in the kickoff invite.

Quick ask: when you place the S3 export, can you include a small mapping file that links queue id -> friendly name? Makes the baseline easier.

See you on Monday — I'll be on the call and bring the acceptance template.

Cheers,
